title: Interim Derating of the Aft Secondary Distribution Box Cabin Outlet Feeders

issue.reason: Original issue of the interim cabin outlet feeder derating dossier.

abstract: A protective derating of the aft cabin outlet feeders in the secondary distribution box, applied as a stop-gap while a permanent thermal solution was designed for the aft equipment rack.

sections.reason: Thermal survey of the aft secondary distribution box during a hot-day ground test found the cabin outlet feeder terminals running 18 degrees above their qualification limit with all cabin outlets loaded. The condition only appears on the ground with the packs at maximum and the aft galley loaded, which is why it had not appeared in flight test. Six aircraft in service showed discoloured terminal insulation at their first heavy check. A permanent answer needed a new box ventilation path, so an interim derating was released first to protect the fleet.
sections.description: The cabin outlet feeder protection in the aft secondary distribution box is derated from 16 A to 12 A per outlet group, and the outlet group allocation is rebalanced so that the aft galley and the aft cabin outlets no longer share a feeder. The harness assembly D2450122851975 is retained but two of its terminations are moved to the spare positions, the connector HAR83831-56 is replaced by an item with the revised keying, and screws EN248527-04 are used at the new terminal positions. The box bus bar 403XU2 and the outlet harness 9177PC5 keep their identifiers. Revised detail is on drawing D24501217521. Work is done at the aft equipment rack in zones 244 and 252.
sections.effects: No mass change. Available cabin outlet power in the aft cabin falls by 25 per cent, which the cabin crew procedure covers by a placard limiting simultaneous galley insert use. No dispatch impact. The change is interchangeable in both directions. Wiring manual content for the aft distribution has to be re-issued because the group allocation changes, and the illustrated parts figure needs the revised connector.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00312 in November 2019 and retrofitted through Service Bulletin CRN-24-1009 at line level. The derating is an interim measure and is expected to be withdrawn once a permanent ventilation path for the aft equipment rack is available.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00312, no line impact

title: Interim Derating of the Aft Secondary Distribution Box Cabin Outlet Feeders

issue.reason: Background note added recording that this change lowered demand rather than raising capability, and that the aft feeder run was never re-rated with it.

abstract: A protective derating of the aft cabin outlet feeders in the secondary distribution box, applied as a stop-gap while a permanent thermal solution was designed for the aft equipment rack.

sections.description: The cabin outlet feeder protection in the aft secondary distribution box is derated from 16 A to 12 A per outlet group, and the outlet group allocation is rebalanced so that the aft galley and the aft cabin outlets no longer share a feeder. The harness assembly D2450122851975 is retained but two of its terminations are moved to the spare positions, the connector HAR83831-56 is replaced by an item with the revised keying, and screws EN248527-04 are used at the new terminal positions. No dispatch impact. The change is interchangeable in both directions. Wiring manual content for the aft distribution has to be re-issued because the group allocation changes, and the illustrated parts figure needs the revised connector. It is worth stating plainly what this change did and did not do: it lowered the demand placed on the aft outlet feeders and left their capability exactly as built. The run between the distribution box and the cabin outlets was not re-rated, and nothing in this dossier claims that it was.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00312 in November 2019 and retrofitted through Service Bulletin CRN-24-1009 at line level. The derating was an interim measure and was withdrawn once the ventilated box standard became available. That standard restored the box outlet rating; because this change had reduced demand rather than raised capability, the feeder run itself was never revisited on either occasion, and the run rating remains the one the aircraft was built with. This note is recorded here so that a later reader following the supersession chain finds the explanation at the point where it belongs rather than reconstructing it.
